deadline.value: Chemistry accepts PhD applications all year, but international applicants seeking funding should target the college-wide President's PhD Scholarship rounds: 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 or 1 Mar 2027 (23:59 UK time). The department's own scholarships (deadline 30 Nov 2026) are for home-fee students only.
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: Applications are accepted throughout the year. We strongly recommend that candidates apply early to increase the chances of securing funding and supervision.
The date for submission of this documentation is Monday 30th November 2026.

supervisor.value: You find a Chemistry supervisor whose research matches your idea and contact them to discuss it before you apply online. President's PhD Scholarship applicants must already have a supervisor's agreement.
supervisor.quote: To search for opportunities based on your own research idea, identify a supervisor whose objectives best match your idea and contact them to discuss your research ideas before you apply online

also.quote: You must have made contact with a supervisor in an academic department at Imperial College London who has agreed to supervise your research project.

funding.value: PhD funding comes from EPSRC, industry, scholarships and self-funding. Departmental scholarships and most advertised studentships are for home-fee students only, so Indian applicants usually rely on the competitive President's PhD Scholarship (open to all nationalities) or external scholarships.
funding.quote: Funding for these students comes from a diverse range of sources, including the EPSRC, industry, scholarships and self-funded students. | This scheme is only eligible to applicants who have home fee status.

also.quote: This competitive scheme has higher than usual eligibility requirements, attracting candidates that show excellent academic performance and promising research potential.

entry_route.value: The minimum is a 2:1 (upper second class) or equivalent degree in a relevant field, so a bachelor's can be enough; some advertised studentships ask for a master's.
entry_route.quote: Upper second class (2:1) or equivalent degree in a relevant field

also.quote: The position is available to candidates holding, or about to hold, a Masters degree in Chemistry

notes: Apply for 'Chemistry Research (PhD)'. The 2:1 entry rule comes from Imperial's draft PhD course page (dev-sites), as the live department page gives no grade. The department admits 50-60 PhD students a year.
